meta.title: x/tools/gopls: modernize slices.Delete suggestion not considering uint type
meta.fix_ref: golang/tools@5a46e4d95cb7 (gopls/internal/analysis/modernize/slicesdelete: convert index type if needed; CL 671735)
meta.build_notes: Both built and run with go1.24.4 (golang.org/dl, under temp/lsp_servers/go-sdks; toolchain.json): the local go1.27 cannot build v0.18.1, go1.24.0 (current when v0.18.1 was tagged, 2025-02-24) cannot build v0.19.0 (its go.mod requires go >= 1.24.2), and go1.24.4 was the current Go release when v0.19.0 was tagged (2025-06-10). The fix merged 2025-05-16.
meta.notes: The slicesdelete pass passed the uint32 indices of append(s[:i], s[i+1:]...) to slices.Delete, whose indices are int. The fix converts the index expressions (int(i), int(i+1)), so the post-fix build still offers a fix, a valid one.

settings_note: The modernize analyzer is on by default in both builds; the reporter ran the modernize command, which runs the same analyzer.

files.source: issue body, 'What did you do?' code block

files.note: a module around the file (the reporter used gopls v0.18.1 and gives no go.mod); go 1.24 (slices needs go1.21)

repro.steps: Open main.go. The slicesdelete pass reports 's = append(s[:i], s[i+1:]...)' with i of type uint32 ('Replace append with slices.Delete'). Apply its fix. Reported: 's = slices.Delete(s, i, i+1)' fails with 'cannot use i (variable of type uint32) as int value in argument to slices.Delete'. Probe: a fresh session on the edited text must report no error the original did not have.

attempts.summary: Run 2026-09-23T09:0x (this case revision): v0.18.1 offered the slicesdelete fix and the result 's = slices.Delete(s, i, i+1)' failed with 'cannot use i (variable of type uint32) as int value' (3/3); v0.19.0 reported no slicesdelete diagnostic at all (verdict invalid, 'no code_action matching the spec was offered'). Cause: v0.19.0 disables the whole slicesdelete pass (EnableSlicesDelete = false in modernize/slicesdelete.go, because slices.Delete clears the vacated slots, golang/go#73686), and v0.20.0 keeps it disabled; it returns in v0.21.0 as a separate analyzer that is off by default. So the release after the fix cannot show the fixed behavior, and no release pair isolates the fix: pre-check 3 (the route exists in the post-fix build) fails. No second attempt.
attempts.verdict: invalid (post-fix release has the pass disabled)
